_note: Patient-friendly explainers used in handouts. Clinical advisor reviews before use.
conj_viral: An infection of the clear layer over the white of the eye, caused by a virus. It spreads easily and usually gets better on its own in 1 to 2 weeks.
conj_bacterial: An infection of the clear layer over the white of the eye, caused by bacteria. It spreads easily.
conj_allergic: Redness and itching caused by an allergy. It is not contagious.
subconj_hemorrhage: A small burst blood vessel on the white of the eye. It looks alarming but is usually harmless and clears on its own.
dry_eye: The eye surface is not staying moist enough, which causes irritation.
hordeolum_chalazion: A blocked oil gland in the eyelid that causes a lump.
pterygium_pinguecula: A growth on the white of the eye, often linked to sun and wind exposure.
lens_opacity_cataract: The lens inside your eye may be getting cloudy (cataract). This is common and can be treated with surgery. An eye specialist needs to check it.
keratitis_ulcer: An infection or sore on the clear front window of the eye. This needs urgent care by an eye specialist.
uveitis: Inflammation inside the eye. This needs urgent care by an eye specialist.
angle_closure: Pressure inside the eye has risen suddenly. This is an emergency and needs care by an eye specialist right away.
other_unclear: Your clinician will explain the findings.
